messages.author: 5cdc3cec34f427f1
messages.subject: Iterating within file names
parts:
How would you go about iterating within file names so that each time my model runs it saves output with a different file name (i.e., matrix-[x].RData for my example below). Also, what would be the best format to save  two-dimensional data arrays so that they can be stacked and averaged together? Let me know if I'm not being clear enough, thanks!

for(x in 1:10){
dataset<-array(runif(50*25,1,100),c(50,25))
save(dataset,file="matrix.RData")
}

messages.author: 056871a2010712cd
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Iterating within file names
parts:
Hi Greg,
Try the paste function.

> test=character(10)
> for (x in 1:10) { test[x] = paste("matrix-", x, ".Rdata", sep='')}
> test
 [1] "matrix-1.Rdata"  "matrix-2.Rdata"  "matrix-3.Rdata"  "matrix-4.Rdata"
 [5] "matrix-5.Rdata"  "matrix-6.Rdata"  "matrix-7.Rdata"  "matrix-8.Rdata"
 [9] "matrix-9.Rdata"  "matrix-10.Rdata"

Then just pass save() the variable test[x] inside the for loop where you'd usually specify a file string, ie:
save(dataset, file=test[x])

HTH,
Christopher Aden

messages.author: b35e99045f6c74c2
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Iterating within file names
parts:
Or, more concisely: 

paste0("matrix-", seq_len(10), ".Rdata")

Note that this is ok only when concatenating parts of a file name. Directories should be combined with file.path, as this is more portable. For example:

file.path("test", paste0("matrix-", seq_len(10), ".Rdata"))

Vince
